headline: React Native Consulting: What a Consultant Does and When to Hire One (2026)
description: What React Native consulting covers, when a consultant beats hiring a full team, what a good engagement looks like and the questions to ask before you sign.

itemListElement.name: React Native Consulting: What a Consultant Does and When to Hire One (2026)

mainEntity.name: What does a React Native consultant do?

acceptedAnswer.text: They review architecture and performance, plan migrations, set up release pipelines, advise on technology choices and support in-house teams. The output is a decision, a plan or an unblocked team more than a finished product.

mainEntity.name: When should I hire a React Native consultant instead of an agency?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you already have engineers and need senior judgement on a specific problem or decision. If you need a product built from scratch with no team of your own, a development team is the better fit.

mainEntity.name: How long does a consulting engagement last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Typically days to a few weeks, with a defined question and a defined end. Longer support can follow, but it should be a choice and not the default.

mainEntity.name: Can a consultant work with my existing developers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Code review, pairing and working inside your existing tools and process are a normal part of consulting, and the aim is to leave your team able to continue alone.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a consultant before rebuilding my app?

acceptedAnswer.text: An independent review before a rebuild is usually worth it. Rebuilds are expensive, and many problems that prompt them can be fixed in the existing codebase.
